 S/o Mogalaya,

 Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the motorcycle Bhagyamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108024897/
1 bearing Reg. No. KA-40-EG-0405 asserting that on 21.08.2022 when walking in front of shop of Seenappa, near Nimmalakunte gate, M.G. Road, Chikkaballapura, rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA- 40-EG-0405 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura and as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 72 years, used to earn Rs.400/per day by working as Coolie.

3. Regarding accident Chikkaballapura Traffic Police registered crime No.59/2022 against the driver of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EG-0405 on 22.08.2022.
4.
In spite of service of the notice of the petition through RPAD and Court, respondent No.1- insurance company remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 appeared through his Advocate, filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation, income,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 09.08.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 21.08.2022 at about 5.00 p.m. opposite Seenappa Shop, M.G. Road, Chikkaballapura town, Chikkaballapura, she met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the rider of the TVS Ntorq bike bearing registration No.KA-40-EG-0405 as alleged?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?

7. On 01.03.2024, 26.03.2024, 04.07.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 10 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.10.
8.

On 03.02.2025 the learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 filed notes of arguments along with copies of insurance policy pertaining to TVS Ntorq bike bearing registration No.KA-40-EG-0405, driving licence, RC and aadhaar card of respondent No.2-owner of the TVS Ntorq bike bearing registration No.KA-40-EG-0405.
9. I have perused the notes of arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.2 and perused the records.

10. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Bhagyamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108024897/
2 Issue No.1 ...

sentences.text: In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.2,15,430/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from 23.01.2025 as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 1. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 21.08.2022 when walking in front of shop of Seenappa, near Nimmalakunte gate, M.G. Road, Chikkaballapura,
rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EG-0405 rode the same negligently,
dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
12.
In the written statement respondents No.2- owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EG-0405 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 are the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.59/2022 registered by Chikkaballapura Traffic police, against rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EG-0405 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC on the basis of the statement of petitioner recorded on 22.08.2022 at about 10.55 a.m. at District hospital by the police.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.5 and 6 are the copies of notice under Sec.133 of IMV Act by investigating officer to respondent No.2 and reply issued by Prakash- respondent No.2.

Ex.P.6 is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is the copy of wound certificate in which reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner are noted as RTA on 21.08.2022 at 5.00 p.m. near Nimmakalakunta, Chikkaballapura taluk while the patient was walking on the road and hit by unknown two- wheeler.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Chikkaballapura police, in crime No.59/2022 against Shivarudraiah S/o Shankaraiah - the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EG-0405 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337,338 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act.
In the police records name of the petitioner is noted as a pedestrian and injured of the accident.
14. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records and oral evidence of PW.1 regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 21.08.2022 at 17 hours when petitioner was walking in front of shop of Seenappa, near Nimmalakunte gate, M.G. Road, Chikkaballapura, Shivarudraiah - rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-40- EG-0405 rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

Bhagyamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108024897/
3 15.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered swelling over right leg, ROM of right leg, abrasion over frontal region, took treatment at Government hospital,
Chickaballapura as inpatient for a period for 13 days, by spending Rs.1,20,000/-, and as on the date of accident being aged about 72 years used to earn Rs.400/-per day by working as Coolie.
16.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

17. Wound certificate, medical bills shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of both bones of right leg, lower 1/3rd abrasion over right wrist, took treatment at Government Hospital,
Chickaballapura 18.
In the wound certificate age of the petitioner noted as 60 years.
In the copy of Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10 the date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 01.01.1950.
Medical bills shows that the petitioner has spent Rs.4,430/- for treatment.

19. Considering nature of the injuries suffered in the accident, length, place and treatment taken for those injuries, I award Rs.60,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.4,430/- towards treatment charges, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, nourishment charges, Rs.96,000/- (Rs.12,000 x 8) loss of income during treatment period, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
20. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.2,15,430/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 23.01.2025 as compensation.

21. The copy of the policy bearing No.990292123750111925 available in the file shows that as on the date of accident motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-EG-0405 had insurance coverage with respondent No.1.
In the reply marked at Ex.P.4 the respondent No.2- Prakash noted identification number of DL of Shivarudraiah S/o Shankaraiah.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of accident respondent No.2 has not violated any terms of the policy.

Hence I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EG-0405 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.2,15,430/- (Rupees Two lakhs fifteen thousand four hundred thirty only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 23.01.2025 to petitioner towards compensation.

The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-EG-0405 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
